userMessages.text:
# OAuth session lifecycle across services

Our browser application uses an external OAuth provider while keeping application sessions under our control. The browser starts login through the web application, which asks the auth gateway to create a short-lived state and PKCE challenge in the session store before redirecting to the provider. The provider authenticates the user and returns an authorization code to a dedicated callback service. The callback validates state, exchanges the code using the PKCE verifier, and sends the provider tokens to an encrypted token vault.

The auth gateway maps the provider identity to an internal account, writes an auditable login event, and issues the browser a secure, HTTP-only application session cookie. Requests enter through the API gateway, which validates the application session and passes only the internal user identity and authorization context to downstream services. Provider access tokens are retrieved by a token broker only when a downstream integration needs one; they never reach the browser or general application services.

When a provider token nears expiry, a refresh coordinator takes a per-account lock, refreshes it once, rotates the stored refresh token, and wakes concurrent callers with the new result. An invalid refresh revokes the application session and requires login again. Explicit logout, administrator revocation, and provider revocation notifications all invalidate active sessions and cached authorization context. Failed state checks, token exchanges, refreshes, and revocations go to the security audit stream without exposing token values.
